newsitem.title: USA: CME live, feeder cattle close higher but off highs.
newsitem.headline: CME live, feeder cattle close higher but off highs.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures closed higher but off best levels posted late as profit taking and evening of positions ahead of Friday's USDA Cattle Inventory report developed, traders said.

Some selling linked to the recent skid in boxed beef prices also trimmed gains. Choice heavy-weight boxed beef value quoted at $95.75 per cwt by USDA at midday was at its lowest level since May 6, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.500 cent per lb higher to unchanged with February up 0.425 at 64.400 cents. October through distant February posted new contract highs earlier.

Futures shot up early on demand prompted by oversold status, talk of cash beef values bottoming and bullish indications on the upcoming USDA Cattle Inventory Report. But beef prices slipped further at midday and cattle futures gains were pared late.
Trading is turning choppy ahead of the USDA data.

"There is a certain amount of indecision amongst traders about what we are faced with here" said Tom Tippens with Professional Cattle Consultants Inc, of the inventory report and the cash market. He said expectations for the report were already largely in the market.
Deferred contracts rose to new highs early on continued support from estimates ahead of the report which indicated shrinking total U.S. cattle supplies, traders said.

Analysts' projections on the inventory report averaged 98.1 percent of last year, or 101.83 million head, for total U.S. cattle numbers on January 1. Actual numbers estimated ranged from 100.9 million to 103.8 million head or 97 to 100.2 percent of a year earlier.

Feeder cattle ended 0.225 to 0.475 cent per lb higher with March up 0.400 at 69.400 cents. April, June and September through November posted new contract highs earlier before paring gains along with live cattle. April's posted a new high of 70.200 cents.

Feeders were influenced most by the pending inventory report. The report was expected to point to tighter feeder supplies this year, especially after reports of large death losses and possible calving problems due to snow storms and bitter cold weather this winter, they said.

E.D.&F. Man sold February live cattle late after early buying by R.J. O'Brien, RBH, Cargill Investor Services and Prudential Securities. R.J. O'Brien bought March feeders late after selling early while Refco was a buyer.
In live cattle options, wire houses sold February 64 calls late, pit sources said.
